text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- In Parliament yesterday Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy noted that the credit-rating agencies Standard & Poor and Moody's had both given more positive assessments of the Hungarian economy in recent months. @
- Free Democrat President Ivan Peto said his party's parliamentary group was surprised by a statement that the government would submit a proposal for amending the act on privatisation.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs and his Czech counterpart agreed Monday in Prague to extend visas to 90 days for citizens of both countries instead of the present 30 days.
- Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti flew to Finland Monday.
- The Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism announced import-export figures for the first three quarters yesterday. @

- A National Bank of Hungary report on the banking sector shows that a total of 39 banks were operating on June 30 this year, 31 of them commercial banks, seven specialised financial institutions and one investment bank. The banks' combined balance sheet showed pre-tax profits of 43.5 billion forints at that time, 54.3 percent more than a year earlier.
- Consumer prices rose an average of 1.4 percent in October. Year-on-year inflation stands at 21 percent.
- A new electrical furnace inaugurated yesterday at the Diosgyori Acelmuvek steelworks could bring the company out of the red by next year. @
- Yachtsman Nandor Fa is returning to Sables d'Olonne, France, cutting short his ill-fated entry in the Vendee Globe round-the-world race, after a Panamanian tanker severely damaged his boat.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The economic cabinet decided Monday to calculate the remaining Russian state debt owed to Hungary at 58.5 percent of the current dollar rate of exchange.
- President Arpad Goncz is due to visit Ukraine November 14-16. @
- The pharmaceutical production company Human Rt. achieved pre-tax profit of 552 million forints in the first nine months on net sales of 9.6 billion forints.
- Pick Szeged Rt.'s first nine months' consolidated balance sheet shows after-tax profit of 1.68 billion forints, at least 33 percent up on the same period of last year.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Magyar Suzuki Rt. achieved revenues of 36 billion forints from the sale of 9,360 cars in the first nine months.
- Unicbank will change its name to Raiffeisen Unicbank Rt. on January 1 next year. @
- The canning factory Csabai Konzervgyar Rt. has been purchased by a consortium of financial investors.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Ten Iraqi refugees began a hunger strike Monday at the Ferihegy airport temporary shelter, seeking appropriate meals instead of pork liver pie, which goes against their religious beliefs.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Police, the tax authority and customs guards will coordinate their next moves against organised crime. @

- The Tax Office, at the request of the national police commander, has begun to investigate the Police Foundation to see that it has not received support from criminals, or from companies against whose executives proceedings have been launched.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
